findings:
🔵 [setsid-wait-fallback-lazy-resolve] CUT/FOLLOW-UP If `_setsid_wait_worker_sid` exhausts its ~1s poll (20×50ms) before the forked `setsid --wait` child has called setsid(), it falls back to `rp`, the supervisor pid, which is not a pgid in a non-job-control shell; the later `kill -SIG -$rp` is then a harmless ESRCH no-op and the bound is silently unenforced while `timeout_enforced` stays `true`. Safe (never reaches dispatcher pgid) and needs sustained scheduler starvation of a fork+setsid, so excluded; hardening would be to re-resolve the leader inside `_watchdog_signal_worker` at fire time when `WORKER_SID`'s sid≠pid.
🔵 [arm-cancel-microrace-orphan-sleep] CUT/FOLLOW-UP If `_cancel_worker_watchdog` sends TERM to the watchdog subshell after it spawned the sleeper but before `trap` is installed / `.sleeppid` is written, the sleeper is orphaned; the `pkill -f hetero-wall-watchdog-<tag>` sweep catches it on setsid hosts (argv[0] is renamed and the pre-exec `bash -c` cmdline also carries the tag), but on the no-setsid fallback branch it is a plain `sleep N` the sweep cannot match. Fallback-only, bounded to `secs`, and the 5× zero-sleep stray test exercises the common branch, so excluded.
🔵 [deadline-coincident-exit-fired-litter] CUT/FOLLOW-UP When the worker exits within the same instant the sleeper wakes, the watchdog can pass `[ -f "$tok" ]` just before cancel unlinks it, then create `<tok>.fired` after cancel already removed it and send a group signal to an already-reaped pgid (ESRCH); result is one stray `.fired` tmp file and, in the mirror ordering, a `timed_out: true` verdict for a worker that finished on its own at the deadline. Sub-millisecond window with no live-process impact, so excluded.
🔵 [set-m-fallback-side-effects] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The no-setsid fallback enables `set -m` shell-wide and never restores it, so later background jobs in that dispatcher (heartbeat, watchdog subshell) get their own pgroups and bash may print job-status notices on stderr. Only reachable on hosts with neither systemd-run nor util-linux setsid; excluded as fallback-only, could be scoped with a saved/restored `$-` check.
🔵 [caller-source-vs-campaign-preflight-order] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `TIMEOUT_SOURCE="caller"` is assigned after `run_strict_contract_preflight` but before `run_campaign_projection_preflight`; if the campaign preflight ever sets `TIMEOUT_SOURCE` only when empty, a campaign wall would be shadowed by `caller`. Not verifiable from the diff and not the Mission-contract mechanism named in the spec; the contract suite is in the Verify list, so excluded.

evidence=(1) enforced-iff-explicit is code-backed: arming is gated on `-n TIMEOUT_SOURCE`, which is only set by contract preflight or the new `TIMEOUT_SUPPLIED==1 && -z TIMEOUT_SOURCE → "caller"` line, so the bare 9m default never arms, manifest writes `timeout_source:"default"`/`timeout_enforced:false`, and `assert_r1_default_not_enforced` asserts exactly that; (2) plain no-contract `--timeout` yields the distinct value `caller` (asserted in `assert_timeout_kill_result` and documented in the OUTPUT comment), so `caller_within_wall` is no longer overloaded; (3) every path establishes isolation BEFORE the wait: cgroup via SCOPE_UNIT + `systemctl --user kill --signal`, setsid --wait via `_setsid_wait_worker_sid` which returns `rp` only when sid==pid (no-fork) and otherwise accepts a child solely when that child's own sid==pid, bounded 20-iteration poll with `kill -0` early break, plain/detached via `setsid env … &` (no fork in a non-job-control shell, so rp is the session leader) or `set -m` + pgid read as the no-setsid fallback; (4) self-kill guards: `$$` inside the subshell is the dispatcher (or detached-child) pid, `_self_pgid` is its pgid, both compared before `kill -SIG -$target`, r6 removed the bare-pid fallback so no non-leader/recycled pid can be signaled, and `assert_r6_no_bare_pid_fallback` proves a live same-pgroup non-leader survives (RED at 9d50f31 shown);
